Fit a variable-order transition tree

Source: R/context_tree.R
context_tree.Rd

context_tree() fits a variable-order transition tree to a set of sequences. The tree, known in the literature as a prediction suffix tree (Ron, Singer & Tishby, 1996) or a variable-length Markov chain (Bühlmann & Wyner, 1999), describes how the next state of a process depends on the states that precede it, while letting the amount of history that matters differ from one history to another. Each node of the tree is a context, or pathway: the most recent states, read from oldest to newest ("A -> B -> C"). The root holds the marginal distribution of states; its children condition on the last state, their children on the last two states, and so on. The tree shows how much of the past is needed to predict what comes next, and along which pathways a longer history changes the prediction.

It counts every context of up to max_depth states that occurs at least min_count times and estimates, for each, the conditional distribution of the next state, smoothed so that unobserved continuations keep a small probability. Sequences may be given as a wide table or matrix (one row per sequence, one column per time point), a list of character vectors, a long event log (one row per event; name the state column in action), or a fitted network object from tna or Nestimate that carries its sequences. With group, or with a grouped network object, one tree is fitted per group over a shared set of states. With the default floor smoothing, the fitted counts and probabilities match those of the PST package (Gabadinho & Ritschard, 2016). It returns a transitiontrees object, or a transitiontrees_group with one tree per group.

The tree is returned unpruned: every context that clears min_count is kept. Use prune_tree() to retain only the contexts whose prediction differs from that of their shorter suffix, tune_tree() to choose max_depth, min_count and the smoothing scheme by cross-validation, and tree_pathways() or as.data.frame() to read the fitted contexts as a table. Group differences are tested with compare_groups(), and the stability of individual pathways with bootstrap_pathways().

Usage

context_tree(
  data,
  max_depth = 5L,
  min_count = 5L,
  smoothing = "floor",
  alphabet = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  block = NULL,
  actor = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  action = NULL,
  order = NULL,
  session = NULL,
  time_threshold = 900
)

Arguments

data

Sequences: a wide data.frame or character matrix (one row per sequence, one column per time point), a list of character vectors, a long event log (with action), or a tna or Nestimate model object that carries its sequence data. NA, "" and the TraMineR codes "%" and "*" mark positions without an observation and are dropped. Numeric matrices are not accepted; convert them to character first.

max_depth

Longest context, in states, that the tree may contain. Default 5.

min_count

Minimum number of occurrences for a context to become a node. Default 5.

smoothing

Smoothing scheme for the next-state probabilities: a method name or a list of the method name and its hyperparameters. Methods are "floor" (default; ymin = 0.001, rule = "interpolate" or "cap"), "laplace" (alpha = 1), "kneser_ney" (discount = 0.75), "witten_bell" and "jelinek_mercer" (lambda = 0.5). See smooth_tree().

alphabet

Character vector of states. NULL (default) uses the states observed in data (for a network object, its node labels). Supply it when new data may contain states unseen here.

weights

Non-negative weight per sequence, one per row or list element of data. NULL (default) fits unweighted.

group

Grouping for one tree per group: a vector with one value per sequence, the name of a column of data (long format) or of a network object's metadata. NULL (default) fits a single tree.

block

Optional block (stratum) identifier in the same forms as group, kept with the fitted group and used by compare_groups() for a stratified permutation test. Default NULL.

actor, time, order, session, time_threshold

Long-format arguments passed to prepare_input(): the column identifying whose events form a sequence, the timestamp column, an ordering column, a session column, and the gap in seconds that starts a new session (default 900). Each defaults to NULL.

action

Name of the state column of a long event log. Giving it reshapes data with prepare_input() before fitting. Default NULL (data is already in sequence form).

Value

An object of class transitiontrees, the fitted tree. Read it through its accessors: as.data.frame() or tree_pathways() for one row per context, state_frequencies() for the state counts, model_fit() for the log-likelihood, information criteria and perplexity, and n_nodes() for the number of contexts. With group, or a grouped input, an object of class transitiontrees_group: one transitiontrees per group, in group order, summarized by summary() with one row per group and flattened by as.data.frame() to one row per group and context.

Conditions

transitiontrees_bad_input when max_depth or min_count is not a single valid number, data has an unsupported type or no usable sequence, a named column is absent, weights, group or block do not have one entry per sequence, a network object carries no sequence data, or the smoothing specification is invalid.

References

Bühlmann, P., & Wyner, A. J. (1999). Variable length Markov chains. The Annals of Statistics, 27(2), 480-513. doi:10.1214/aos/1018031204

Gabadinho, A., & Ritschard, G. (2016). Analyzing state sequences with probabilistic suffix trees: The PST R package. Journal of Statistical Software, 72(3). doi:10.18637/jss.v072.i03

Ron, D., Singer, Y., & Tishby, N. (1996). The power of amnesia: Learning probabilistic automata with variable memory length. Machine Learning, 25(2-3), 117-149. doi:10.1023/A:1026490906255

See also

prune_tree() and smooth_tree() to refine a fitted tree; tune_tree() to choose its settings; tree_pathways() to read it; plot.transitiontrees() to draw it; compare_groups() to compare groups.

Examples

# Wide sequences: one learner per row, one time point per column
tree <- context_tree(trajectories, max_depth = 3)
tree

# One tree per achievement group over a shared set of states
groups <- context_tree(group_regulation_long, actor = "Actor",
                       time = "Time", action = "Action",
                       group = "Achiever", max_depth = 2)
summary(groups)
